title: Joint Design-and-Estimator Minimax Risk for the Independent-Margin Probability of Superiority
banked_reason: The proved leading constant, sharp n^-3/2 order, coefficient interval, count-law reduction, and fixed-family diagnostics support a narrower theorem-note contribution; the evaluated sharp correction and matching original-record rule remain open.
gap_reasons: No such reduction is established, and even obtaining it would leave the variable-width weak-order game unsolved.

proof_attempt_summary: Two D0 solve rounds retained the full-cube leading constant 1/3 and n^-3/2 correction-order bracket, and added exact design symmetrization and fixed-marginal coupling diagnostics. The focused retry disproved localization for the frozen scalar checkpoint windows; it does not disprove localization for every adapted rule or existence of the requested minimax coefficient. The evaluated correction, matching original-record attaining rule, and optimized-design comparison remain open; no Lean formalization or certification was performed.
tldr: Independent-margin superiority is the diagonal-inclusive comparison of the two empirical potential-outcome margins. On the full bounded paired-schedule class, we prove that the unrestricted, fair-independent, and balanced-complete minimax risks all have leading constant \(1/3\). On both parity subsequences, the normalized \(n^{-3/2}\)-scale improvement has liminf at least \(4/(3\sqrt3)\) and limsup at most \(4/\sqrt{15}\). For the specified fixed-width logistic grid, we separately prove uniform limits for the information, conditional empirical-target variance, score-regression defect, cell phases, and truncated tails. The exact correction coefficient, a matching total unrestricted procedure, and the optimized comparison of fair independent and balanced complete assignment remain open.
gap: Chen--Li defines the exact marginal effect and develops complete-randomization inference for specified comparison estimators. Existing rank variance and distribution-specific power results do not optimize all designs and all point rules on fixed paired schedules.
fill: The sharp-risk question joins a total original-record estimator construction to a matching finite-target lower certificate and an evaluated local saddle. The named-design question then measures the precision cost, if any, of enforced balance after each estimator is optimized.
